mcqs.q: Which archaeological site in Tripura features monumental 7th-9th century rock-cut Shaivite carvings, known as the 'Angkor Wat of the North-East'?
mcqs.exp: Unakoti ('one less than a crore') features massive stone reliefs, prominently the 30-foot head of Shiva.

mcqs.q: Neermahal, eastern India's only lake palace built in 1930 by Maharaja Bir Bikram Kishore Manikya, is situated in which lake?
mcqs.exp: Neermahal combines Hindu and Mughal architectural styles in the center of Rudrasagar Lake.

subtopics.name: Geography
subtopics.summary: Location, borders, physical terrain, and major river systems of Tripura.

facts.title: Capital & Geographic Scope
facts.content: The capital is Agartala. Tripura covers a geographic area of 10,491 sq km across 8 administrative districts.

facts.title: Major Rivers & Drainage Systems
facts.content: Key river systems flowing through the region include: Howrah, Gomati, Manu, Khowai, Feni.

facts.title: Geographical Landscape & Highlights
facts.content: Surrounded on three sides by Bangladesh. Ruled for centuries by the Manikya dynasty. Home to Ujjayanta Palace, the colossal rock-cut carvings of Unakoti ('Angkor Wat of North-East'), and Queen pineapple.

subtopics.name: History & Culture
subtopics.summary: Historical formation, classical/folk dances, and vibrant festivals of Tripura.

facts.title: State Formation & Language
facts.content: Tripura was formally instituted on 21 January 1972. Official language(s): Bengali, Kokborok, English.

facts.title: Dance Forms & Traditional Arts
facts.content: Celebrated traditional and folk dance forms: Hojagiri (performed on an earthen pitcher), Garia, Lebang Boomani.

facts.title: Major Festivals & Celebrations
facts.content: Prominent cultural festivals: Kharchi Puja (worship of 14 deities), Garia Puja, Neermahal Water Festival.

subtopics.name: Government & Polity
subtopics.summary: Constitutional leadership, administrative structure, and state symbols of Tripura.

facts.title: Governor & Constitutional Head
facts.content: The current Governor is N. Indrasena Reddy.

facts.title: Chief Minister & Administration
facts.content: The Chief Minister of Tripura is Manik Saha.

facts.title: High Court Jurisdiction
facts.content: Judicial jurisdiction falls under High Court of Tripura (Agartala).

facts.title: Official State Symbols
facts.content: State Animal: Phayre's leaf monkey | State Bird: Green imperial pigeon | State Flower: Nageshwar | State Tree: Agarwood.

subtopics.name: Economy & Agriculture
subtopics.summary: Natural resources, minerals, industrial clusters, and agriculture in Tripura.

facts.title: Mineral Wealth & Natural Resources
facts.content: Principal minerals and resources: Natural Gas, Glass sand, Clay.

facts.title: Economic Profile & Industries
facts.content: Tripura plays a vital role in India's economy through key agricultural production, manufacturing corridors, and services.

subtopics.name: Places, Monuments & Tourism
subtopics.summary: Heritage landmarks, national parks, and tourism attractions in Tripura.

facts.title: Historic Monuments & Cultural Sites
facts.content: Prominent monuments and heritage landmarks: Ujjayanta Palace, Neermahal (Water Palace in Rudrasagar Lake), Unakoti Rock Sculptures, Tripurasundari Temple.

facts.title: National Parks & Protected Areas
facts.content: Key protected conservation areas: Clouded Leopard National Park (Sepahijala), Rajbari National Park (Bison).

subtopics.name: State Schemes & Awards
subtopics.summary: Prominent welfare schemes, civic initiatives, and state honors of Tripura.

facts.title: Key State Welfare Schemes
facts.content: Notable welfare initiatives and government programs: Mukhyamantri Chaa Sramik Kalyan Prakalpa, Tripura Gramin Bank microcredit.
